source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Facilitate a fair structured discussion that identifies issues and workable solutions","B":"Automatically side with the nurse who has the longest relationship with the manager","C":"Terminate one or both nurses before attempting any structured conflict-resolution process","D":"Ignore the conflict because interpersonal problems usually resolve without intervention"}}
source_row.rationale: A nurse manager's appropriate role in addressing staff conflict includes facilitating a structured, fair conversation between the involved parties, helping identify underlying issues and potential solutions, while maintaining professionalism and objectivity — proactive conflict management supports a healthier work environment and better patient care outcomes.
source_row.source_detail: Mutual-support/conflict tools emphasize structured, respectful problem-solving rather than favoritism or avoidance; current TeamSTEPPS curriculum; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: Two staff nurses on a unit have an ongoing interpersonal conflict affecting team dynamics, and one nurse privately asks the manager to simply side with them since they've worked together longer than with the other nurse. The nurse manager's appropriate role instead includes:
